en: ...{a}, do you think you're cool?
Yes, I'm cool
No, I'm not cool
Neither

...I see.
That's a safe answer.
They say people who answer like that secretly think they're pretty cool, deep down.
I'm sorry for asking you something so strange.
May I ask you one more strange thing?{p}
{a}, do you like rain?
I like it
I hate it
Neither

...So you hate rain.
I love it.
The rainy season most of all.
When the hydrangeas bloom.
The air is so humid that its lukewarm touch soaks right into your skin.
My shirt clings wetly to my body and doesn't even stir in the wind, and it makes me truly feel that I'm wearing clothes. I find that so lovely.
And in the rainy season, it could start raining at any moment, couldn't it?
Weather that threatens rain but never brings it.
A sun shower, when rain suddenly pours from a cloudless blue sky.
Rain sends shivers of delight through me.
I'd like to live in a world where the rain never stops.
Sometimes the thought just comes over me.{p}
Tell me, {a}, when it rains, do you use an umbrella?{p}Or do you like to go without one and get soaked?
I use an umbrella
I don't use one
It depends on how hard it's raining

Oh, I see.
What a waste of lovely rain.
Rain is a blessing from heaven.
God goes to the trouble of sending it down just for us, and yet...
I never use an umbrella.
Never, no matter how hard it pours.{p}

With rain falling from all across the sky, I turn my face up to the heavens.
And I catch the rain with my whole body.
It's wonderful.
Because it feels so good.
You should try it once yourself.
When the rain is light, it turns into a mist that tickles my skin and stirs my senses.
When the rain is heavy, it beats down hard on my body with a fierce roar.
The rain is alive.{p}

Heh heh... Maybe you can't understand this pleasure.
But the story I'm about to tell may be just perfect for someone like you, who hates rain and shuts out lovely rain with an umbrella.{p}By the way, {a}, do you keep a spare umbrella at school?
I do
I don't
Not all the time

Of course.
I think that's how most people who use umbrellas are.
Especially in the rainy season.
Even if you keep a spare umbrella at school, when it suddenly starts raining, you end up using it, don't you?
And then, when the next day is sunny, it seems people just forget to bring an umbrella back.
Not many people keep three or four spare umbrellas at school.
If anyone did, they'd simply be lazy, wouldn't they?
So in the rainy season, rain or shine, you'd have to carry an umbrella every single day.
But that's not easy to do.
Umbrellas are such a nuisance.
When it looks like it couldn't possibly rain, hardly anyone walks around carrying an umbrella, right?
And even if they do, they'll just end up leaving it somewhere.
That's why in the rainy season, you often see people waiting out the rain by the shoe lockers.{p}

How stupid of them.
It's lovely rain, so they should just get soaked to the skin on the way home.
People clicking their tongues, looking up at the sky with openly disgusted faces, as if they hated heaven itself...
I can't understand people like that.
People like that ought to just die.
{a}, you're not that kind of person, are you?
...Heh heh heh.
They're just awful, people who wait out the rain.{p}
But you know, for a girl, that's also the perfect chance for romance.{p}

Once, there was a girl named Yukari Tachibana.
She was in love with someone.
His name was Hiroshi Tsukahara.
Tachibana was by no means an unattractive girl.
If anything, she was cute.
But she wasn't the kind of flower that stands out from all the rest.{p}

Tsukahara, on the other hand, was incredibly good-looking.
He had features that hardly looked Japanese, a fine, chiseled face, just like a model.
Mind you, I never actually saw either of them, so I don't know what they looked like.
So of course he was popular.
He always had a following of girls around him, squealing over him.
Frankly, Tsukahara didn't have a very nice personality.
He took it for granted that girls would fall for him, and he acted like a star.
So the other boys hated him.
But Tsukahara didn't care about that. If anything, it gave him a sense of superiority, and it went straight to his head.
Honestly, he was a nasty piece of work.{p}

It was the rainy season, and Tsukahara had no umbrella, so he was waiting out the rain.
The very situation I just described.
At that moment, by chance, none of his followers were around.
And Tachibana had an umbrella.
A big red umbrella.{p}

"...Um, are you waiting for someone?"
"Nah, not really.
It started raining, so I've got no choice but to wait it out.
I don't want my hair getting wet.
Man, what a pain. Stupid sky."
With that, he glared up and cursed the sky, as if he hated heaven itself.
"...Um, here.
Would you like to share it with me?"
Tachibana held out her red umbrella.
"Oh, sure.
Thanks.
You're a lifesaver.
Which way are you headed?"
Shameless as he was, Tsukahara was never going to turn down an offer like that.
"...Um, which way are you going, Tsukahara?"
"Huh? You know my name?
Wow, I'm flattered.
Oh, my place is that way."
The direction Tsukahara pointed was the opposite way from the station Tachibana was heading for.
"Oh, me too."
But Tachibana said it with a smile.
It was her big chance, after all.
A little lie like that didn't bother her at all.{p}

And so the two of them walked shoulder to shoulder under one umbrella.
Tachibana was so happy.
She wished time would just stop right there.
She even thought that as long as this happiness lasted, she didn't care what became of her.
"So, what's your name?"
"It's Yukari Tachibana."
"Oh, Yukari.
Hey, Yukari, have we met somewhere?"
"...No. I think this is the first time."
"Huh. And you still knew who I was.
How come?"
That's just the kind of person Tsukahara was.
If it had been me, I might have killed him.
But Tachibana was an earnest girl, you see.
"...Oh, well, I've been a fan of yours, Tsukahara."
"Wow, that makes me happy.
Thanks."{p}

With that, Tsukahara put his arm around Tachibana's shoulder and pulled her close.
For Tsukahara too, a girl like her was something rare.
Most of the girls around him were the pushy type who squealed over him, after all.
So a girl like Tachibana seemed fresh to him.
"You're really cute, Yukari.
I wouldn't mind making you my girlfriend."
Of course, he was only half serious.
It was a line he said to every girl, without a second thought.
But to her, it was different.
Tachibana's heart was ready to leap out of her chest.
She was so happy, so very happy, she thought she might lose her mind.
And she prayed that this wasn't a dream, and said thank you to God.{p}

"If you want, why don't you come over to my place now?
I want to get to know you better, Yukari, and I think we'd really hit it off."
Tachibana was never going to say no.
She accepted his invitation in a heartbeat.
The Devil's invitation.{p}

Tell me, {a}.
What do you think of this guy Tsukahara?{p}Maybe he's a lot like you, hmm?
I can't stand the guy
All guys are like that
I'd rather not get involved in other people's business

Tachibana went along with Tsukahara.
And she went into his house.
His parents weren't home.
Well, he knew that, which is why he lured her there, I suppose.{p}

She was a butterfly caught in a spider's web, wasn't she?
Even if she'd tried to escape, he would never have let her go.
But Tachibana had no need to escape.
She never even thought of escaping.
Because she was happy too.
Being alone with Tsukahara... there was no greater happiness for her.
By then, Tachibana did whatever Tsukahara told her.{p}

Those were truly happy days.
At school too, she stuck to Tsukahara's side.
But his followers didn't get angry, and they didn't complain to Tachibana either.
They just watched from a distance, sneering.
As if they already knew how it would end.{p}

And that end came soon enough.
It took Tsukahara less than a week to get bored of Tachibana.
In the end, he probably just couldn't get along with a serious, boring girl who did nothing but whatever he said.
Tachibana was dumped, just like that.
Tachibana didn't understand what had happened.
She couldn't grasp where she stood right away.{p}

After all, Tsukahara had suddenly turned cold toward her.
It was worse than cold. He ignored her, or rather, he started looking at her as if she were something filthy.{p}

On the surface, he kept up appearances and smiled, but Tachibana loved him, and she could read his heart like an open book.
'You're in my way. Hurry up and get out of my sight.' That's what it said.
Tachibana was earnest, and he was the first boy she had ever gone out with.
So she couldn't understand why he had changed so suddenly.
He wouldn't answer her calls, and when they met at school, he wouldn't even speak to her.
He'd trade a few smooth words with her, then go straight off to the other girls.{p}

Still, as time went by, she came to face the truth: she had been dumped.
She had only been toyed with.
But she couldn't forget Tsukahara.
That's how much she loved him.
And she made herself believe that the week they spent together had been a dream, a gift from God.{p}

And so she went back to watching him from afar.
That way, she wouldn't get in his way, and he wouldn't come to hate her.{p}
...Tell me, {a}.{p}What do you think of Tachibana, being like that?
I think she's sweet
I think she's a bit odd
I think she's scary
I think that's normal

...Thank you for answering my question.
I'm sorry. I'll go on with the story.{p}

But God does love his little pranks, doesn't he?
After all, he gave Tachibana one more chance.
It was toward the end of the rainy season.
Maybe Tsukahara just wasn't the type to keep a spare umbrella at school.
He was waiting out the rain again.
All by himself.
And Tachibana had an umbrella.
A big blue umbrella.{p}

Tachibana hesitated.
She couldn't just stand by and watch Tsukahara in trouble.
But if she showed herself, he might not like it.
In the end, though, she couldn't bear to watch him struggle any longer, and she rushed out.{p}

"...Um, please use this umbrella."
At first he looked annoyed to see her, but he soon smiled.
"Oh, thanks. Wanna walk home together?"
She hadn't meant to walk home with him.
Even so, he pushed her into sharing the umbrella with him.{p}

She felt terribly awkward.
Even so, he went on chattering as he pleased.
"Man, I'm sorry.
I just haven't had any time lately.
I've been busy, y'know, with this and that. You get it, right?
I just wanna be nice to everybody.
It's not like I'm into anyone or anything.
See? So it's not like I started hating you, Yukari..."{p}

As he said that, he suddenly tried to kiss her.
"Please stop."
Startled by the sudden move, Tachibana refused him.
She still loved him even now, but she already knew he had only been toying with her.
She believed that kissing was wrong unless two people loved each other.
So she shoved Tsukahara away.{p}

Frankly, he was taken aback.
No girl had ever turned him down before.
At first he tried to laugh it off, but his pride had been badly wounded.
So he attacked her.
"Don't you screw with me!"
Tachibana was shocked.
The Tsukahara she had thought so kind was coming at her with a monstrous face.{p}

She swung the umbrella around wildly.
"Stop!
Please stop!"
Suddenly she felt a dull impact in her hands.
The hands holding the umbrella abruptly grew heavy, as if it had caught on something.
"Gyaah..."
...Tsukahara was groaning.{p}

When she looked, the tip of the umbrella was stuck in his left eye.
The blood pouring out of it was carving a red pattern into the blue umbrella.
"...Y-you bastard.
I'll fucking kill you!"{p}

Terrified beyond words, Tachibana squeezed her eyes shut and just kept thrusting the umbrella out.
Not knowing what she was doing, she thrust it out again and again.{p}

Each time, she felt it strike something heavy.
The feel of it plunging into something heavy and soft...{p}

After a while, Tachibana fearfully opened her eyes.
Tsukahara lay sprawled in front of her.
He didn't move a muscle; his face and body had been stabbed all over, and he lay dead, drenched in blood.
His face was a pulpy mess, as if birds had pecked at it, with flaps of flesh peeled back here and there.
When she looked, the blue umbrella was dyed bright red too.
But strangely, she wasn't afraid.
She had fallen flat on her bottom; leaning on the red-stained blue umbrella, she staggered to her feet.
Then she stabbed the umbrella into Tsukahara's utterly still corpse, again and again.
Humming a tune as she did.
And then she killed herself.{p}

They say she was found dead with the umbrella stabbed into her own throat.
They say a person normally can't drive an umbrella into their own throat.
It would hurt too much to go through with it, wouldn't it?
But she saw it through.
When she was found, they say her throat had been pierced clean through, from front to back.
She must have thought she had to die.
And she must have thought that the more pain she felt, the more her sin would be atoned for.
That's why she endured the pain and drove the umbrella in, I suppose.
That's what I think.{p}

It was all written off as a breakup gone wrong: the woman killed the man, then killed herself to follow him.
Even though that's not what really happened.{p}

...The strange thing, though, was the murder weapon left at the scene: the blue umbrella.
At first, they say, everyone thought it was a red umbrella.
Why? Because even though it had been raining, the blood on the umbrella hadn't washed off.
They say the color had set in, as if the umbrella had been dyed through.{p}

...And that's the end of Tachibana's story.
...But they say that after Tachibana died, something strange began to appear.{p}

On rainy days, they say, a high-school girl with an umbrella stands quietly by the school gate.
As if she's lying in wait for someone who has no umbrella.
And they say that sometimes she's holding a blue umbrella and a red umbrella.
I wonder who on earth she could be.
...Though I have a fair idea.{p}

{a}, you might want to be careful.
I'm sure Tachibana has had enough of men like Tsukahara by now.
Next time, she might fall for a boy like you.
...But you said you thought Tachibana was a strange girl, didn't you?
You'd better be careful.
The more devoted and earnest a girl is, the less you can tell what she'll do when you make her angry.
Whatever you do, be careful when a girl confesses her feelings to you.
If you think you can just play around with her for fun... If it were me, I'd kill you.
Heh heh...
Now, shall we hear the next person's story?{p}

My, you're quite sure of yourself.
Anyone with ordinary sensibilities wouldn't go around calling themselves cool.
And yet you......That's a little surprising.
But you know, that kind of attitude isn't good.
I don't like it.
...Well, never mind.
Let me ask you one more thing.{p}

My, that's not true.
I think you're not bad at all.
Either way, you're far more likable than someone who calls themselves cool.
I like people like that, heh heh...
May I ask you one more strange question?{p}

I see, so you like the rain.
Come to think of it, I know a story about someone who loved the rain, just like you.
His name was Hata, I believe.
Hata was a student at this school.
He was earnest and kind, and his grades were decent, upper-middle or so.
But he wasn't popular with girls.
As for why... it's a little hard to say.{p}

He was by no means handsome.
Girls just can't help judging by appearances, can they?
To me, that seems nothing but foolish.
But the girls, unable to see the beauty inside him, paid Hata no attention at all.{p}By the way, {a}, are you interested in girls?
Yes, I'm interested
I'm not interested at all

Hata was the same.
But he had his friends.
So even if the girls wouldn't give him the time of day, he didn't get too anxious about it.
There were other things he loved, too.
And among the many things he loved, just like you, {a}, was the rain.{p}

He loved the rain.
So much that he didn't mind going without an umbrella, even in a downpour.
Then, one day...
That day, a fine drizzle had been falling since morning.
To him, that hardly even counted as rain.
He had an umbrella his family had forced on him, but he couldn't be bothered to open it, so he walked along getting wet.{p}

Then he saw a girl sheltering from the rain under the eaves of a shop.
She was looking up at the sky, lost and on the verge of tears.
Her helpless expression was so cute that Hata went over to her without thinking.
When she noticed him, the girl flinched and backed away.
Flustered, Hata pressed his umbrella into her hands.{p}

"Please use this."
The girl looked at him in surprise.
He could see himself reflected in her large, glossy eyes.
Hata turned red.
But it would be odd to take the umbrella back now, wouldn't it?{p}

Practically flinging the umbrella at her, Hata broke into a run.
The girl watched his back for a long, long time.{p}

The next day, it was raining too.
On his way home from school without an umbrella, Hata met her again.{p}

Smiling sweetly, she held out the umbrella she had borrowed from Hata.
"Y-you don't need it anymore?"
Hata's voice came out high and shaky.
She smiled and nodded.
That smile was warm and gentle, overflowing with affection.
She likes me.
...That's what Hata thought.{p}

When he headed home with his umbrella back, he realized she hadn't said a single word.
But he thought nothing more of it than that she must be shy.
After that, the girl began waiting for Hata on his way home.
Strangely, though, only on rainy days.{p}

What's more, she was always in front of the same shop.
They would stand there and talk... though he was the only one who talked.
When he'd said all he had to say, she would see him off and he'd head home. That happened several times.
Even so, Hata was happy.
Just seeing her smile made him happy from the bottom of his heart.
But people are greedy creatures, aren't they?
Just once, Hata wanted to try this thing called a date.
So one day, he asked her out.{p}

"Will you go on a date with me?"
...Like that.
She fell silent and looked down.
When he asked what was wrong, she didn't answer.
She just bit her lip, looking troubled.
Hata had been sure she would say yes, so it came as a shock.
She had always listened happily to whatever he said.
So Hata had believed she liked him.
But come to think of it, he had never actually heard it from her own lips.
Burning with shame and shock, Hata lost his temper.
"W-were you just making fun of me?"{p}

Her wet body was melting into sludge.
There was no trace left of her lovely face.
She melted away without the slightest resistance, like ice doused with hot water.
Right before Hata's eyes, she vanished without a trace.
He didn't understand what had happened.
But she hadn't been human.
Hata screamed and ran home.{p}

But... she was there.
Wearing her usual meek smile.{p}

Then he caught his breath and looked up.
There was a small shop in front of him.
And under its eaves was... her.
Had she gotten there ahead of him?
Hata lost his head.
And to get away from her, he dashed out into the street.{p}

...After he was hit by the car, they say Hata was struggling desperately.
As if he were frantically trying to escape from something.
The witnesses said he had suddenly dashed out into the street, though.
...That's right.
Strangely, it seems no one but Hata could see her.
What was she, really?
Why was Hata the one she clung to?
I don't know...
Maybe strange things come out on rainy days.{p}

You'd better be careful too, {a}.
If you go wandering around just because you like the rain, something strange might take a liking to you.
Heh heh...
That's the end of my story.
Now, who's next?{p}

My, you're not?
{a}, you're a late bloomer, aren't you?
Or......you're not going to tell me you prefer boys, are you?
...Well, never mind.
Anyway, most high-school boys are interested in girls.{p}

I'll ask you one more time, so pick one or the other.
Now, do you like the rain?{p}Or do you hate it?
I like it
I hate it

My, you don't use one?
That's right, that's the correct answer.
Going out of your way to keep the precious rain off with an umbrella is just stupid.
You understand that, don't you?
I'm so glad.
To meet a kindred spirit in a place like this.{p}

Honestly, saying you hate the rain... that was cruel of you.
...No, I'm not angry.
Quite the opposite, I'm glad.
You like getting wet in the rain too, don't you?
Yes, I understand.
I knew it from the moment I first saw you.
That's right, you like the rain.
Of course you do.{p}

I'm sure we'll get along well.
After all, we both love the rain.
In that case, shall I tell you a story about the rain?
You'll be pleased, won't you, {a}?
Have you ever seen people standing by the shoe lockers on a rainy day, saying they're waiting out the rain?
There are plenty of people like that, aren't there?{p}

Hmm, so you play it by ear?
You say that, but maybe you're really just a sloppy sort who uses an umbrella when you have one and walks home wet when you forget it.
Oh, now you look annoyed.
I'm joking, just joking... heh heh.
Well then, may I ask you something?{p}{a}, do you keep a spare umbrella at school?
I do
I don't

They say plenty of romances get their start thanks to an umbrella.
You know, like in those girls' comics.{p}

So you don't.
Lots of people are like that, aren't they?{p}

Boys especially.
That's why, in the rainy season, I often see people waiting out the rain by the shoe lockers.{p}

My, how admirable.
But not everyone in the world is like you, are they?
Boys especially. I'd think it's rare for one to keep a spare umbrella at school.
But you know, for a girl, that's also the perfect chance for romance.{p}

Oh, really.
So that's the kind of person you are, {a}.
A man who's a disgrace to the human race.
You can't understand the pain in other people's hearts, can you?
You won't notice it until the same thing happens to you.
I can't forgive people like that.
I can't forgive them.{p}

And you call yourself a journalist?
Do you really think you can get by in the newspaper club without taking an interest in people?
I can't tell my story to someone so careless.
Why don't you answer a little more seriously?
Come on, answer me.{p}I asked what you think of Tsukahara.
I can't stand the guy
All guys are like that

Hmm, is that so.
Well, if that's how you feel, that's fine.
But God does love his little pranks, doesn't he?
After all, he gave Tachibana one more chance.{p}

Maybe Tsukahara just wasn't the type to keep a spare umbrella at school.
He was waiting out the rain again.
All by himself.

A big blue umbrella.{p}

In the end, though, she couldn't bear to watch him struggle any longer, and she rushed out.{p}

At first he looked annoyed to see her, but he soon smiled.
"Oh, thanks.
Wanna walk home together?"{p}

She hadn't meant to walk home with him.
Even so, he pushed her into sharing the umbrella with him.{p}

She felt terribly awkward.
Even so, he went on chattering as he pleased.
"Man, I'm sorry.
I just haven't had any time lately.
I've been busy, y'know, with this and that.
You get it, right?
I just wanna be nice to everybody.
It's not like I'm into anyone or anything.
See? So it's not like I started hating you, Yukari..."{p}

As he said that, he suddenly tried to kiss her.
"Please stop."
Startled by the sudden move, Tachibana refused him.
She still loved him even now, but she already knew he had only been toying with her.
She believed that kissing was wrong unless two people loved each other.
So she shoved Tsukahara away.{p}

No girl had ever turned him down before.
At first he tried to laugh it off, but his pride had been badly wounded.
So he attacked her.
"Don't you screw with me!"
Tachibana was shocked.
The Tsukahara she had thought so kind was coming at her with a monstrous face.{p}

She swung the umbrella around wildly.
"Stop!
Please stop!"
Suddenly she felt a dull impact in her hands.
The hands holding the umbrella abruptly grew heavy, as if it had caught on something.
"Gyaah..."
...Tsukahara was groaning.
When she looked, the tip of the umbrella was stuck in his left eye.{p}

...Ow!
Just then, a faint pain shot through my eye.
My left eye, too, just like in the story.
Iwashita went on with her story without noticing.{p}

"The umbrella was driven in deep.
The blood pouring out of the wound was carving a red pattern into the blue umbrella."{p}

Throb... throb...
What's happening to me?
The pain in my left eye was getting stronger and stronger.
No, this was more than pain.
It was hot.
It felt like it was burning.
What...
What on earth is this?{p}

"Tsukahara was past caring about anything now.
He pulled the umbrella's tip out of his left eye and tried to lunge at her.
Tachibana was so terrified that she shut her eyes tight and just thrust the umbrella out.
Not knowing what she was doing, she thrust it out again and again and again."{p}
It hurts!

It hurts!
Searing pain shot through my body, all over.
It felt like something was being stabbed into me.
I crumpled to the floor.
"Heh... Does it hurt?
That's the pain Tsukahara felt."
...I realized Iwashita was smiling down at me.{p}

"I figured it out while we were talking.
You're the same breed as Tsukahara.
If I let you live, some other girl, somewhere, is going to end up crying.
So I'm going to kill you."
...What?
But Iwashita hadn't done anything to me, had she?
So why this pain...?
As if she had read my mind, Iwashita bent down over me.{p}

"I've put Tachibana's curse on you...
You'll feel the pain Tsukahara felt, and you'll die the same way he did."
Her eyes were drawn up at the corners, and her smile was not that of the Iwashita I'd seen until now.
It was something more evil...... like a witch.{p}

"That's right... I'm a witch.
A witch who protects girls from wicked men..."
Iwashita's smile grew wider.
No... that's ridiculous.
But this pain was covering my whole body.
I was slowly losing consciousness.
I don't want to die like this...
I tried to struggle.
But I couldn't even lift a finger anymore.
As I was swallowed up by agony and darkness, Iwashita watched me, delighted......{p}

That's right.
Tachibana really was a devoted girl.{p}

That's exactly why she was content just to watch him.
But Tsukahara wasn't willing to leave it at that.
Having her watching him all the time? No way was he going to put up with that.
What a horrible man.
So he gathered together the girls who always hung around him...{p}

One day, Tachibana was called out by a group of girls.
And they surrounded her.
"We hear you've been following Tsukahara around?"
"Can't you tell you're a pain in his neck?"
...They all laid into Tachibana, one after another.
Poor Tachibana couldn't even talk back.{p}

Of course she was mortified.
She hadn't done anything wrong, after all.
But to think Tsukahara found her that much of a nuisance.
And that he'd gone and told other people.
Her pride was torn to shreds.
Tachibana went home... and slit her wrists.{p}
